# Frontier reset: scientific checkpoint, 7 October2026

The strongest research-enabling advance is a smaller explicit detector and exact learner for finite-state noncommutative algebraic models. The strongest separate foundational lead is a threshold-repetition theorem for arbitrary commuting-operator strategies. Both have complete written derivations and multiple internal reconstructions. Neither has external validation, compiled formal verification or established historical novelty. No revolutionary breakthrough is claimed.

## 1. Exact representation acquisition

For n symbols and a proper characteristic-zero recognizable series with at most m hidden states, let T_i be the explicit Volterra matrices of dimension2nm. Our new theorem is

    f !=0  implies  f(ell T_1,...,ell T_n)!=0
    for some integer ell in {1,...,m}.

All evaluations exist because the matrices are jointly strictly lower triangular. This is a universal deterministic hitting set whose construction reads only n,m. One direct-sum tuple has dimension2nm². The prior construction in this cycle used a length marker of dimension approximately n²m⁴. For acyclic representations, one unscaled tuple of dimension2nm already suffices when its full matrix output is read.

The proof uses the released finite-word hyperlogarithm independence, but replaces its scalar multiplicity argument with a bivariate Volterra kernel. A covariant rational row-span argument finds a nonzero diagonal derivative before order m. Degree bounds and Cauchy interpolation make it visible in dimension2nm. A new scalar-parameter degree bound then reduces cyclic faithfulness to m fixed rescalings. This last step was derived by root and independently reconstructed by four workers. Root also reconstructed the complete primary monodromy proof of finite-word independence.

The boundary is equally concrete. The nonzero proper series

    AB-B(I+A)^-1A(I+B)

has leading commutator AB-BA, yet vanishes on the unscaled Volterra operators J_1,J_2 on EVERY formal input, and hence at every finite truncation. Increasing the matrix size cannot repair that cyclic alias. Scalar grading supplies the missing information.

## Statement

Let f be a proper recognizable noncommutative formal series with at most m states:

    f_w=uB_wv,   f(x)=u(I-sum_i B_i x_i)^-1 v.

There are no inverses of singular constant terms. For every n,m>=1 let T_i be the same explicit lower triangular Volterra matrices of dimension d=2nm used in the acyclic theorem. Then

    f!=0  =>  f(ell T_1,...,ell T_n)!=0 for some ell in {1,...,m}.

Every evaluation exists, because the T_i are jointly strictly lower triangular, so the series truncates regardless of cyclic B_i. The single block diagonal tuple direct_sum_(ell=1)^m ell T_i therefore detects all such series at dimension2nm^2. This replaces the previous universal length marker of dimension about n^2 m^4. It does not turn an unmarked single scalar tuple into a faithful cyclic model: an explicit five-state alias shows that is false.

# Independent root gate: full-matrix Volterra fingerprints

7 October2026. Scoped verdict: PASS of the new argument, conditional on the source's finite-word hyperlogarithm independence. Three other workers separately reconstruct the analytic and acquisition interfaces. This is internal mathematical support, not external or formal validation; priority remains UNKNOWN.

## Precise positive result

Over any characteristic-zero field, let f be a noncommutative polynomial with an acyclic m-state linear representation f_w=uB_wv, where all B_i are strictly upper triangular. For n variables, the explicit rational matrices

    (T_i)_(r,q)=(-1)^(r-q-1)/(r i^(r-q)) for 0<=q<r<2nm

(and zero otherwise) satisfy f(T)!=0 whenever f!=0. The generator reads only n,m. It requires the FULL evaluated matrix. For a formula of source size s with m<=2s, dimension4ns suffices. This improves the source's quadratic-in-state first-column construction by changing its response interface.

Root read and independently derived every step of `notes/frontier_experiments/cycle19/LINEAR_DIMENSION_CANDIDATE.md`:

1. Set A(z)=sum B_i/(z+i)=P(z)/q(z), degP<=n-1, q(0)!=0, and G'=AG,G(0)=I. For zero constant term, f(J)a is the Volterra integral with kernel K(z,t)=uG(z)G(t)^-1 A(t)v. The left-letter order is essential and checks. Nonzero finite-word faithfulness implies K!=0.
2. Rows R_0=u,R_(j+1)=R_j'+R_jA have numerators Z_j of degree<=j(n-1) over q^j. The first rational dependence among at most m+1 rows makes their preceding span invariant under the covariant derivative, even when dependence coefficients have poles. It follows that some diagonal derivative b_j(t)=R_j(t)A(t)v is nonzero with j<m.
3. That derivative has order at most(j+1)(n-1). Thus K(t+x,t), and therefore K(z,t), has a nonzero homogeneous component of degree ell-1<=nm-1. The invertible linear substitution preserves total order; it does not assert any individual coefficient survives cancellation.
4. For K_(ell-1)=sum_b c_b z^(ell-1-b)t^b, the entry in row q+ell,column q of f(T) is sum_b c_b/(q+b+1). Taking q=0,...,ell-1 gives an invertible Cauchy matrix. The largest required row2ell-1 fits dimension2nm. This proves detection with no numerical rank argument or multiplicity estimate.
